correctness.rationale: The 256 four-mer words give 136 reverse-complement orbits, of which exhaustive exact word tests admit 56 vertices (12 singleton, 44 two-word). The 420-edge graph enforces precisely the remaining pairwise overlap and Hamming constraints. Every valid codebook uniquely corresponds to a weighted clique. The exact base-case/branching recurrence counts all cliques and yields coefficients (1,12,88,288,584,760,688,424,160,32). A structurally separate direct-word backtracker independently enumerates 3037 codebooks and 32 nine-word maximizers, and checks four size-eight symmetry orbits. Both standalone programs were executed on the included files.

originality.rationale: King 2003 treats Hamming and reverse-complement distance, not reverse-complement closure plus cross-bifix exclusion. Blackburn 2013/2015 treats unrestricted non-overlap maximum and constructions, not Hamming separation or the combined polynomial. Related previously indexed results on n=4 RC-closed non-overlapping extrema without Hamming distance, on n=4 GC-balanced comma-free codes, and on n=3 reverse-complement-closed non-overlapping spectra concern distinct domains or constraints and do not determine this complete size spectrum. Searches found no exact equivalent indexed table; historical uniqueness remains a risk.

value.rationale: The three constraints independently correspond to framing synchronization, double-strand closure, and detection of one aligned substitution. At length four, fixed and paired RC-orbits coexist and give 32 optimal designs in four symmetry types with two distinct optimal compositions. The complete cardinality polynomial measures all viable codebook sizes, not just the optimum, and is not implied by separate classical code-size bounds. Its scope is a natural complete finite classification with a reproducible exact graph certificate, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice. Practical biochemical quality is not asserted.
